display.purpose: The h1 on an individual example page. The catalog index never uses it.

headline.purpose: Example name at the top of each catalog section; the strongest type on the index.

subtitle.purpose: h3 inside guidance blocks and the keyboard panel.

section-title.purpose: Supporting h2 headings outside the catalog index.

lede.purpose: The single-line description beneath an example-page title.

body.purpose: Prose and panel lists, capped at 72ch.

summary.purpose: The single muted line under each example heading, capped at 58ch.

label.purpose: Control labels and the reset button; compact enough to keep two control rows above the fold.

group-name.purpose: DATA and APPEARANCE row markers; the only uppercase chrome type.

readout.purpose: Live monospace numeric value beside each slider.

breadcrumb.purpose: The compact page-position line above example titles.

code.purpose: Code blocks and API reference tables.

chart-tick.purpose: SVG axis labels; px so they scale with the viewBox, not the root font size.

chart-month.purpose: Uppercase month boundary ticks inside charts.

shadows.name: spine-ring
shadows.purpose: The only box-shadow in the system. Rings the semantic-feed marker so the dot stays visually attached to the spine at any axis width. Structural, blurless, offsetless.

shadows.name: reserved-shadow-token
shadows.purpose: Declared as --tl-color-shadow in :root for both themes but consumed nowhere. Reserved, not an invitation to start shadowing.

motion.name: fast
motion.purpose: The only duration token (--tl-motion-fast). Applied to marker fill/stroke and to input border/background.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The only easing used; state changes settle rather than overshoot.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion collapses all transitions, animations, and smooth scrolling globally.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Control rows become a 4-column wrapping grid; headings collapse to one column; keyboard panel becomes a bottom sheet.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Control rows drop to 3 columns with 0.625rem gaps; SVGs release their desktop height floor; reset stretches.

geometry.name: chart-viewbox
geometry.purpose: Shared SVG coordinate space; plot band spans x 72 to 888.

geometry.name: calendar-viewbox
geometry.purpose: Tighter SVG coordinate space that fits the familiar week-by-day grid without dead space.

geometry.name: responsive-chart-type
geometry.purpose: Chart type scales in SVG user units at narrow widths while geometry reserves the corresponding space.

geometry.name: page-width
geometry.purpose: Single centred column with overflow-x: clip so no chart can push the page sideways.

geometry.name: reading-width
geometry.purpose: Prose cap; example summaries are capped tighter at 58ch.

geometry.name: hit-target
geometry.purpose: Minimum height for form controls, including the reset button; shared site-header actions use 2rem targets.

declaredButUnused.name: --tl-radius-md
declaredButUnused.note: Declared in :root, referenced nowhere. Do not use it to soften new chrome.

declaredButUnused.name: --tl-color-shadow
declaredButUnused.note: Declared for both themes, referenced nowhere. The system is flat.

narrative.overview:
Timelines is a workbench, not a showroom. Twelve real renderers are laid out in one vertical scroll, each with its own controls bolted directly above it, and nothing is put behind glass. There is no hero, no visible wordmark, no card grid, no numbered section decoration, and no narrative copy between examples. An engineer arrives, reads a name and one line of summary, turns two rows of knobs, watches the live SVG respond, and scrolls to the next instrument. The page is the evidence.

The surface is a cool neutral light or dark field with no tonal container ladder: every example sits on the same background and is separated from its neighbour by whitespace and heading hierarchy. Density is compact and instrument-like. Indigo carries every event, marker, and interactive edge; green carries every aggregate magnitude; the chrome is otherwise ink and muted grey. Rectangles are honest rectangles - only the interactive inputs soften, and only by 6px.

Rejections are explicit and confirmed: no hero section, no visible wordmark, no card grid, no section-number decoration, no explanatory prose beyond the one-line summary, no horizontal section rules, and no boxed containers wrapping a chart. Depth is not a tool here. If something needs to read as separate, spacing and typography must do the work.
keyCharacteristics: One vertical scroll containing all twelve live renderers, in order, unwrapped.
Controls grouped as exactly two labelled rows - Data, then Appearance - above the chart they drive.
Cool neutral surfaces (#f7f8fa / #101217) with whitespace instead of section dividers.
Indigo for events, green for aggregates; a third amber only inside stacked composition.
Compact system-sans throughout; monospace reserved for numeric readouts and code.
Flat by default: one structural box-shadow exists in the whole system.

rules.name: The Two-Signal Rule
rules.body: Indigo means an individual event; green means an aggregated quantity. A renderer never swaps them, and no third colour enters a chart unless it is encoding a categorical type.

rules.name: The Whitespace Rule
rules.body: Catalog sections and control groups are separated by spacing and typography, never horizontal rules. Hairlines are reserved for interactive or semantic boundaries.

rules.name: The Wash-Never-Ground Rule
rules.body: #e8eaff is a state tint on small elements only. It never becomes a section, panel, or card background.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: One sans stack carries the entire interface. Monospace appears only where characters are being compared as data: numeric readouts, timestamps, code blocks, and API reference tables.

rules.name: The No Wordmark Rule
rules.body: The site has no visible title or logo. The content is the product; the shared header contains actions only.

rules.name: The Shared Shell Rule
rules.body: Catalog, detail, and documentation pages mount the same site header from src/site-ui.js. Page-specific actions belong in content, not in a competing header.

rules.name: The Uppercase Budget Rule
rules.body: Uppercase is spent on exactly two things: the control-group names and month ticks. Nothing else shouts.

rules.name: The Unboxed Catalog Rule
rules.body: An example is never wrapped in a card, panel, or bordered container. Its only boundary is the whitespace around it.

rules.name: The Controls-Above Rule
rules.body: Controls belong in the same scroll column, directly above the chart they drive, in two labelled rows. They are never docked, floated, collapsed into a drawer, or placed in a sidebar.

rules.name: The Two-Row Rule
rules.body: All controls fall into exactly two groups: Data (what is rendered) and Appearance (how it looks). A new control joins one of them; it does not create a third row.

rules.name: The No-Lift Rule
rules.body: Nothing in this interface floats. Hover changes border colour and fill, never elevation, never translateY.

rules.name: The Square Chrome Rule
rules.body: Page-level surfaces are square. If a container has a radius, it is either something the user manipulates or a sheet anchored to the viewport edge.

dos: Do keep all twelve examples in one continuous vertical scroll, in catalog order, each with its live renderer in the page.
Do put controls directly above the chart they drive, grouped into exactly two labelled rows: Data, then Appearance.
Do mount the shared site header and component heading from src/site-ui.js.
Do separate examples through compact vertical rhythm and clear heading hierarchy.
Do use indigo (#4c5dff) for discrete events and green (#00a57a) for aggregate magnitude, in every renderer, without exception.
Do give every form control the full 2.75rem hit target, including the reset button.
Do style chart internals through the --tl-*-local custom-property contract so appearance controls keep working.
Do keep chart text in px inside the viewBox, and keep chrome text in rem.
Do honour both data-theme and prefers-color-scheme, and keep every colour role present in both themes.
donts: Don't add a hero section, a marketing banner, or a landing intro above the catalog.
Don't author page-local header or theme-toggle markup.
Don't arrange examples as a card grid, and don't wrap an example, its controls, or its chart in a card, panel, or bordered container.
Don't divide catalog sections or control groups with horizontal rules; whitespace carries the hierarchy.
Don't add section numbers, step counters, or decorative ordinals to example headings.
Don't add narrative or explanatory copy between examples; the one-line summary and the detail link are the entire budget.
Don't introduce box-shadow for elevation - the spine ring is the only shadow in the system, and it is structural.
Don't use indigo wash (#e8eaff) as a section or page background.
Don't move controls into a sidebar, a sticky bar, a modal, or a collapsed drawer.
Don't add a third control group; a new control joins Data or Appearance.
Don't soften page-level containers - squares stay square, and --tl-radius-md stays unused.
openObservations: Mobile Appearance rows can end with an empty trailing grid cell when a renderer exposes an odd number of controls; this is acceptable asymmetry in the responsive instrument grid.
The semantic horizontal feed intentionally scrolls and snaps one item at a time on narrow viewports rather than compressing its prose.
Aggregate green first appears below the event-only renderers in the catalog because colour follows data meaning, not viewport composition.
